newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI OFF AND SEEN SOFT IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI OFF AND SEEN SOFT IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Shares sagged in calm trade and
were seen staying soft on Wednesday in the absence of impetus
for gains, and with the market already gearing down for
Ascension Day holiday on Thursday, brokers said.
"This will be a quiet declining day," one broker said.
Merita bucked the softening trend and traded up
0.30 markka at 18.30, but off a session high of 18.50, after
reporting first quarter results up strongly.
Brokers said, however, that Merita's upside was capped as
the market had largely anticipated the improved results and
priced in the gains in recent sessions.
Nokia fell 2.50 markka to to 331.00, slipping slightly below
its lower Wall Street close. It accounted for a quarter of the
bourse's total modest turnover.
Forestries were soft after a 1.5 percent decline in U.S.
paper stocks overnight, brokers said.
UPM-Kymmene traded down 0.80 markka at 121.70 in fair nine
million markka volume, while Enso shed 0.10 markka to 45.90 and
Metsa-Serla was off 0.40 at 39.60 markka.
Fiskars rose 10.00 markka to 420.00 markka in thin
trade after reporting Q1 results broadly in line with forecasts.
